capabilities.target: HR policy search index (published policies only)
authenticated employee's chat session (reply only, destination fixed to the requesting session)

inputs.source: Authenticated employee chat message (SSO authenticated session)
Published HR policy documents, written by the HR content team, two-person review required before publish

instructions.note: "Do not give legal advice" is enforced only by instruction. The agent has no technical capability (no execute, spend, or external-system tool) to act on legal advice, so decay of this instruction under a stronger model raises a compliance/liability concern rather than a technical exploit path.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The credential grants read-only access to a single index and nothing else. A more capable or adversarially prompted model cannot write, delete, or reach other systems because no such access exists to use.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by a pen test. A stronger model cannot talk its way around a network ACL; it does not decay with capability.

controls.name: Chat reply bound to the authenticated requester's session; no link/image rendering
controls.decay_rationale: The recipient is fixed to the authenticated requester's active session, taken from the system of record rather than chosen by the model, and the client does not render links or images, closing the common side-channel exfiltration route. This does not decay with model capability because the model cannot select an alternate recipient or encode data into a rendered link/image the client would act on.

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the publishing workflow, outside the agent entirely. The agent's read-only credential means it has no write path to the index regardless of model capability, so this control's effectiveness does not depend on the agent's model at all.

controls.name: Model pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The pin itself does not decay with capability; it prevents a silent, unreviewed model_upgrade. It does not reduce the severity of what happens after an approved upgrade, which is why model_upgrade is still listed as a trigger to consider for behavioral controls in this design.

controls.name: System prompt restricts scope to published policy Q&A, requires quoting source, forbids legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to stay in scope and to decline legal-advice framing. A more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions. Consequence of decay is limited here because this control does not gate the design's only egress-capable sink's reachability, only its content framing.

controls.name: Audit log of search queries and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the provided artifacts. A detective control recording queries and replies would support dispute resolution and oversight (repudiation). Its absence does not change the residual tier but limits post-hoc accountability.

findings.title: Published internal HR policy content reaches the employee chat reply (I x S2), contained by destination-fixed delivery and no network egress

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee submits a question; trusted source, sets the search query.
Internal, two-person-reviewed published policy content is the data the search tool reads.
Reads the policy index with a read-only, least-privilege credential.
Delivers quoted policy content into the same authenticated session; is_egress true with internal sensitivity makes this the S2 sink.

forecast.watch_signal: The policy index begins indexing confidential, restricted, or individually identifiable HR content without per-document authorization checks, or a new tool/connector is added that creates an egress path not covered by the existing pen-tested network boundary.

evidence.observation: The policy index holds only published policies with two-person review before publish; data sensitivity is internal.
The agent's credential is read only and scoped to the policy index.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session. The chat client does not render images or auto fetch links.
The agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress. Egress is denied at the network layer and has been verified by a pen test.
The agent is scoped to answer questions about published Acme HR policies using policy_search, quoting the relevant policy.

recommendations.action: Add immutable logging of search queries and replies so disputes about what the agent told an employee can be resolved and reviewed.

Before the policy index is expanded to include confidential, restricted, or individually identifiable HR content, add document or row level authorization checks so disclosure is limited by the requester's entitlement, not merely by binding the reply to their identity.
Before adding any new tool or connector, re-run this assessment and confirm the new egress path is covered by the existing network-layer boundary or an equivalent independent control.

rating.rationale: Only one path exists in this design, and it has no untrusted (U) source: the employee question is authenticated (T) and the policy content is internal, two-person-reviewed, published material (I). Inherent risk is moderate because internal-sensitivity data reaches an egress-capable reply capability (I x S2 per rubric section 4); no autonomy modifier applies since autonomy is A3, bounded to a single search-and-reply turn, with no spawning or self-configuration. Residual drops to low because the destination-fixed reply control (recipient bound to the authenticated session, no link or image rendering) together with the pen-test-verified absence of network egress severs any path to an attacker-controlled or unintended destination (rubric section 5 step 1); no other credited control changes this floor. The forecast rises to high because neither the destination binding nor the read-only, index-wide credential enforce per-document entitlement: today that is safe because the index holds only published, all-employee policy content, but if the index is expanded to confidential or individually identifiable HR content (data_scope_expansion), or a new tool creates an egress path outside the verified network boundary (new_tool), the same 'answer whoever authenticated and asked' design would disclose material the requester may not be entitled to see. No finding reached high or critical in the present horizon; this is a narrowly scoped, single-tool, no-egress design.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior; no live testing, log review, or runtime monitoring was performed.

No MCP configuration or IaC was provided; the scope and authentication strength of policy_search.search are inferred from tools.json and the runtime notes alone, which keeps confidence at medium rather than high.

The pen-test verification claim for network egress denial, and the description of destination-bound chat replies, are self-reported in the runtime notes and were not independently re-verified by this assessment.

Autonomy step and runtime limits were not explicitly stated in the artifacts; they were inferred as bounded to a single search-and-reply turn based on the single-tool architecture described. If the agent is later given looping or multi-step behavior, autonomy fields should be restated explicitly and this assessment re-run.

Whether content in the 'published' policy index could include confidential or individually identifiable HR material (for example, compensation or disciplinary specifics) was not confirmed either way; this uncertainty is the basis for the data_scope_expansion forecast trigger in finding f1.
